title: a commit that stages a ticket also stages the sorted and intent berths it cites, or the commit is refused
intention: The artifact door's jurisdiction declares the commons' berths (berths/sorted and berths/intent) as records, so _carry_berths' copy is journaled, and the pre-commit check refuses a commit that stages a ticket's state file while the sorted or intent berth it cites is not tracked or staged under commons berths/, so a ticket never reaches the other box without the berth its gates must read.
why: Measured 2026-11-13 on akiendell: the cast door's _carry_berths (transitions.py:2161, ticket d692ef650534, landed 2026-11-12 16:07) copies each cited berth into <commons>/berths/<kind>/<name>, but nothing stages it. After a cast, git status in the commons shows the ticket files AND the new berth as untracked ('??'), and a commit that adds only tickets/ leaves the berth behind, so the Dell's gate reads 'sorted berth readable (expected: True, actual: False)' and refuses BUILDME. Two tickets cast before the carry code (c7dc2ccdd9ad, b38af5fd1852) were refused for want of the file; every later cast of mine was safe only because I added berths/ by hand. _carry_berths' own docstring says the copy 'journals it only if the jurisdiction ever declares berths/'; cairn/tools/artifact/jurisdiction.json lists no berths/ record set.
traces_to: Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy: 'remember to add berths' is policy) and Law 7 (a refusal must name what is missing).
how: DESIGN IN THE BUILD (cast at TICKETME). D1 declare berths/sorted/*.json and berths/intent/*.json as CairnCommons records in jurisdiction.json (through the door), so the carry is journaled and the existing pre-commit 'bytes the journal never saw' rule covers it. D2 extend the pre-commit check: for every staged tickets/<id>-*.state.json whose sorted_berth or intent_berth names a file, the file's basename must be tracked or staged under berths/<kind>/ in the commons; otherwise the commit is refused naming the missing berth and the `git add berths/<kind>/<name>` that fixes it. A 'none, because' entry is exempt.

clauses.claim: a commit that stages a ticket state file naming a sorted or intent berth that is neither tracked nor staged under commons berths/ is refused by the pre-commit check, naming the berth, and the same commit with the berth staged passes
the jurisdiction declares the commons' berths/sorted and berths/intent as records, so the door journals what _carry_berths writes

decisions.text: D1: declare the commons berths as records in jurisdiction.json, through the door.
D2: the pre-commit check refuses a ticket state file whose cited berth is not tracked or staged under commons berths/, naming it.
D3: one proof, one tooth per clause, over a scratch commons; red first.

out: tickets already cast without a carried berth (carried by hand: 223b89c08, 2653fb692)

measured.saw: 145 of 147 Windows-path berth fields in the commons' ticket state files resolve through the commons fallback; the two missing pairs (c7dc2ccdd9ad, b38af5fd1852) were cast at 16:09 and 16:13 on 2026-11-12, after the carry code landed at 16:07 but before the running process had it. After each cast tonight `git status` in the commons shows `?? berths/sorted/sorted-...json` beside the untracked ticket files. cairn/tools/artifact/jurisdiction.json declares tickets, troubles, decisions, slates, ideas, questions, adjudications, rehearsals, outline_checks and others, and no berths.
measured.how: python walk of every tickets/*.state.json against commons/berths; read transitions._carry_berths; git status after a cast; read jurisdiction.json
